account: On 11 September 2020 the U.S. Food and Drug Administration cleared the Fitbit electrocardiogram (ECG) app for the detection of atrial fibrillation or sinus rhythm only. Fitbit's own summary says that this detection is not recommended for people with other known arrhythmias. By 28 September 2021 Fitbit's product page listed India among the countries where the Sense could run the ECG app. In October 2021 a 55-year-old man in Jamshedpur, India, had palpitations, sweating, anxiety and mild dizziness for half an hour while at work. His Fitbit Sense watch detected an irregular heart rate of 164 beats per minute with irregular rhythm and bizarre QRS morphology. He felt the need to visit a doctor immediately and sought care at Tata Main Hospital. A 12-lead ECG showed tachycardia at 166 beats per minute with bizarre QRS complexes under 130 milliseconds and right axis deviation. Idiopathic fascicular ventricular tachycardia was diagnosed. After adenosine did not reverse the tachycardia, clinicians restored sinus rhythm through electrical cardioversion. They also corrected severe hypokalemia with intravenous potassium. Holter monitoring, echocardiography and coronary angiography excluded structural heart disease. He subsequently received oral verapamil and telmisartan. After four cardiology visits he was reported to be doing well with no further complaints. A case report published in Cureus on 18 July 2023 describes the case and does not give the exact day of the presentation.
